name: Altstadt Rattenberg
kurzbeschreibung: With around 450 residents, Rattenberg is Austria's smallest town and world-famous for medieval alleyways and glassmaking craftsmanship.
beschreibung:
Overview

Covering a total area of barely eleven hectares (0.11 km²) and home to approximately 450 residents, Rattenberg in the Tyrolean Unterinntal is Austria's smallest municipality with town status. Dramatically squeezed between the rugged rocks of the Schlossberg and the banks of the Inn, the town's territory was unable to expand over the centuries. Consequently, the late medieval town layout has remained almost entirely intact to this day. Rattenberg is internationally famous as Tyrol's traditional "Glass Town": numerous demonstration glassblowers, glass cutters, and engravers shape the vibrant artisanal life in the historic alleys.

History & Craftsmanship

The first recorded mention dates back to 1254; Rattenberg received its town charter in 1393. In the Middle Ages, the settlement was a strategically vital transshipment port for shipping on the Inn as well as a key Bavarian customs and border fortress against Tyrol. It was only after the War of the Succession of Landshut that the town permanently fell to Tyrol in 1504 under Emperor Maximilian I. The continuous streetfront is dominated by colorful townhouses in the Inn-Salzach style featuring typical parapet facades, battlements, and arcades. Distinctive monuments include the 12th-century Nagelschmiedhäuser – two double-gabled houses built directly against the rock face of the Schlossberg –, the late Gothic parish church of St. Virgil, and the Augustinermuseum, housed in a former Servite monastery and showcasing outstanding Tyrolean art treasures. In the 19th century, glass finishing sparked a new economic boom: at the heritage company Kisslinger Kristallglas, visitors can watch glassmakers at work right at the furnace free of charge.

Visit & Getting There

The historic center of Rattenberg is designated as a pedestrian-only zone and accessible free of charge throughout the year. Glass studios and boutiques are open Monday through Friday from approx. 09:00 to 18:00 and on Saturdays from 09:00 to 17:00. An accessible panoramic path leads up to the Schlossberg ruins, offering splendid views over the Inntal valley. The town is internationally acclaimed for the traditional Rattenberger Advent on the four Saturdays of Advent, when all electric lights in town are switched off and the alleys are illuminated solely by hundreds of candles, torches, and open fireplaces. By car: via the Inntalautobahn A12, exit 32 Kramsach/Brixlegg, following signs for Rattenberg; generous visitor parking lots (P1–P4) are available outside the town gates, as the historic core is strictly car-free. By public transport: with ÖBB trains (S-Bahn Tirol S4, REX) to Rattenberg-Kramsach station; a pedestrian footbridge leads from the station into the heart of town in just three minutes.

Tips

The entire town center is car-free and features flat paving that is effortlessly navigable with wheelchairs and strollers. The ascent to the Schlossberg ruins via the winding path is also very manageable. Be sure to try the famous Rattenberger Schlosstorte in the traditional pastry shops and allow enough time for a live glassblowing demonstration.
